competences: The learner find outer dimensions from inner dimensions and border widths.
The learner calculate the area of a rectangular border.
languageCompetence: Reads, pronounces, spells and correctly uses: border, outer length, outer width, inner area.
objectives: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to find outer dimensions from inner dimensions and border widths.
By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to calculate the area of a rectangular border.
priorKnowledge: Learners can subtract inner rectangle area from outer rectangle area.
materials: Two border diagrams labelled with inner lengths and border widths
references: P 6 Primary SIX MTC Notes Docx (ecolebooks Com)

steps.content: Learners can subtract inner rectangle area from outer rectangle area. Starter: An inner rectangle is 8 cm long and 5 cm wide, with a 2 cm border on each side. Find the outer length.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher displays two border diagrams labelled with inner lengths and border widths, reviews the prior skill, and asks: "An inner rectangle is 8 cm long and 5 cm wide, with a 2 cm border on each side. Find the outer length." The teacher records learners’ methods and connects them to area of rectangular borders.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners recall the previous skill, read the starter question, and explain which measurements or operations they would use.

steps.content: Rectangular borders: $\text{Shaded area}=\text{outer area}-\text{inner area}$. Area is measured in square units.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes and explains the following worked content: $\text{Shaded area}=\text{outer area}-\text{inner area}$. Area is measured in square units. The teacher demonstrates each substitution or operation, asks learners to explain the units, and checks individual working before moving to the next step.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the given measurements, copy the calculation steps, explain the operation used, and check that the answer carries the correct units.

steps.content: Example: a two-centimetre border: Inner length is $8\text{ cm}$ and inner width is $5\text{ cm}$. The border is $2\text{ cm}$ wide on every side. $\text{Outer length}=8+2+2=12\text{ cm}$. $\text{Outer width}=5+2+2=9\text{ cm}$. $\text{Outer area}=12\times9=108\text{ cm}^2$. $\text{Inner area}=8\times5=40\text{ cm}^2$. $\text{Border area}=108-40=68\text{ cm}^2$.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes and explains the following worked content: Inner length is $8\text{ cm}$ and inner width is $5\text{ cm}$. The border is $2\text{ cm}$ wide on every side. $\text{Outer length}=8+2+2=12\text{ cm}$. $\text{Outer width}=5+2+2=9\text{ cm}$. $\text{Outer area}=12\times9=108\text{ cm}^2$. $\text{Inner area}=8\times5=40\text{ cm}^2$. $\text{Border area}=108-40=68\text{ cm}^2$. The teacher demonstrates each substitution or operation, asks learners to explain the units, and checks individual working before moving to the next step.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the given measurements, copy the calculation steps, explain the operation used, and check that the answer carries the correct units.

steps.content: Example: a three-centimetre border: Inner length is $5\text{ cm}$ and inner width is $4\text{ cm}$. The border is $3\text{ cm}$ wide on every side. $\text{Outer length}=5+3+3=11\text{ cm}$. $\text{Outer width}=4+3+3=10\text{ cm}$. $\text{Outer area}=11\times10=110\text{ cm}^2$. $\text{Inner area}=5\times4=20\text{ cm}^2$. $\text{Border area}=110-20=90\text{ cm}^2$.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes and explains the following worked content: Inner length is $5\text{ cm}$ and inner width is $4\text{ cm}$. The border is $3\text{ cm}$ wide on every side. $\text{Outer length}=5+3+3=11\text{ cm}$. $\text{Outer width}=4+3+3=10\text{ cm}$. $\text{Outer area}=11\times10=110\text{ cm}^2$. $\text{Inner area}=5\times4=20\text{ cm}^2$. $\text{Border area}=110-20=90\text{ cm}^2$. The teacher demonstrates each substitution or operation, asks learners to explain the units, and checks individual working before moving to the next step.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the given measurements, copy the calculation steps, explain the operation used, and check that the answer carries the correct units.

steps.content: An inner rectangle is 8 cm long and 5 cm wide, with a 2 cm border on each side. Find the outer length. For the same 2 cm border, find the outer width. For the same 2 cm border, find the shaded area. An inner rectangle is 5 cm by 4 cm, with a 3 cm border on each side. Find the outer length and width. For the same 3 cm border, calculate the area outside the inner rectangle.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher sets these questions: An inner rectangle is 8 cm long and 5 cm wide, with a 2 cm border on each side. Find the outer length. For the same 2 cm border, find the outer width. For the same 2 cm border, find the shaded area. An inner rectangle is 5 cm by 4 cm, with a 3 cm border on each side. Find the outer length and width. For the same 3 cm border, calculate the area outside the inner rectangle. The teacher checks each learner’s working, marks against these computed answers: 8 + 2 + 2 = 12 cm. 5 + 2 + 2 = 9 cm. 12 × 9 − 8 × 5 = 108 − 40 = 68 cm². Length = 5 + 3 + 3 = 11 cm; width = 4 + 3 + 3 = 10 cm. 11 × 10 − 5 × 4 = 110 − 20 = 90 cm². and supports learners who confuse lengths, areas or units.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners solve the questions individually, show each calculation, compare marked answers, and correct any errors in substitution or units.

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher asks learners to explain their solutions to these questions: An inner rectangle is 8 cm long and 5 cm wide, with a 2 cm border on each side. Find the outer length. For the same 2 cm border, find the outer width. For the same 2 cm border, find the shaded area. An inner rectangle is 5 cm by 4 cm, with a 3 cm border on each side. Find the outer length and width. For the same 3 cm border, calculate the area outside the inner rectangle. The teacher checks the lesson objectives against the written work and assigns correction of the final exercise item.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners explain their calculation methods, state the correct units, and correct the final exercise item after receiving feedback.

source.quote: Calculate the area of the un-shaded part

assessment: Mark the written working for these questions: An inner rectangle is 8 cm long and 5 cm wide, with a 2 cm border on each side. Find the outer length. For the same 2 cm border, find the outer width. For the same 2 cm border, find the shaded area. An inner rectangle is 5 cm by 4 cm, with a 3 cm border on each side. Find the outer length and width. For the same 3 cm border, calculate the area outside the inner rectangle. Check the stated measurements, operations, final answers and units against the answer key.
homework: Correct and fully work this exercise item: For the same 3 cm border, calculate the area outside the inner rectangle.
